The only callers of `PatientService.getAllergies` in the REST module are in `PatientAllergyResource2_0`, which is the `/ws/rest/v1` patient allergy sub-resource. Three methods in it call it, and each could be affected by a change in behaviour:

1. **`doGetAll(Patient, RequestContext)`** (line 165). This is the GET path for `/patient/{uuid}/allergy`. It branches on `allergies.getAllergyStatus()`: UNKNOWN returns 204, NO_KNOWN_ALLERGIES returns an empty list, and SEE_LIST returns the allergies. Any change to status or contents from `getAllergies` changes the response.
2. **`delete(String parentUniqueId, String uuid, String reason, RequestContext)`** (line 211). With no allergy UUID, it loads all of the patient's allergies and voids each one. This is the "delete all, back to Unknown" path, so it depends on the returned collection being complete.
3. **`put(String parentUniqueId, SimpleObject post, RequestContext)`** (line 294). This sets the patient to "No known allergies". It checks `isEmpty()` on the result before calling `setAllergies`, so a change to what `getAllergies` returns for a patient with existing allergies would change whether this throws.

The test class `omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs2_0/PatientAllergyController2_0Test.java` also calls `getAllergies` in about 15 places. Those are tests, not the resource itself, so I've left them out of the list below. They would fail if the behaviour changed.

Outside the REST module, the core callers are `PatientServiceImpl` (`api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/impl/PatientServiceImpl.java`, lines 756–757 and 1483) and `AllergyValidator`. Those are not part of the `/ws/rest/v1` resources, so I haven't listed them.
